newsitem.title: CROATIA: Croatian stocks higher, activity seen rising.
newsitem.headline: Croatian stocks higher, activity seen rising.

text.p: Croatian stocks were mostly higher in livelier trade on Friday and market participants foresaw rising activity with higher share prices in the week ahead as investors returned from summer break.
"I excpect the market to grow significantly," said Ivan Hren of private Ceufin Brokers, adding that prices may not rise at such a fast pace, but that demand would push them up.
"Zagrebacka banka will grow faster because it is tied to London market," he said.
Zagrebacka's GDR, issued at 10 to each share, traded today at $14.13-14 on Seaq International.
* Of eight active issues four rose, two were flat and one was down. Two stocks traded for the first time.
* The most active, Zagrebacka, edged up five kuna to 675 on volume of 6,734 shares.
* Drugs firm Pliva was the biggest gainer, rising 250 kuna to 11,500 on volume of 282 shares.
* Hotelier Laguna gained 10 kuna to 810, trading 59 units.
* Another hotelier Suncani Hvar was also up 4.5 kuna to 45 kuna with 266 units changing hands.
* Confectioner Kras stayed flat at 275 kuna, selling 278 shares.
* Travel agent Atlas and hotelier Zlatni rat traded for the first time, at 195 and 118 kuna each, on volume of 247 and 197 shares.
* Volume almost tripled at 9,274, turnover more than doubled at 8.3 million kuna.
* Weekly turnover lower at 16.921 million kuna.
